title: No new required-story marker replaces the old check mark
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 2 users · 2 browsers · about 15 minutes
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  • [User-B]: a user whose role uses the Tech View work order mode from Roles & Permissions (e.g. a "Technician" role, Settings > Roles & Permissions > the role > Work orders > View mode = Tech view), signed in in a second browser. This is the Simple Flow tech view mode, not the Tech View display on the Work Orders page.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F3 No Story Marker" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset.
  • Work order [WO-1] for this customer: status Approved, two lines — "Line 1" with a tech story and "Line 2" without one.
  • Line names and story text are examples.

Setup

  1. Top menu Customers > New Customer, Name "ZZAUTOTEST F3 No Story Marker" > Save (skip if it already exists). On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty. Record the customer as [Cust-1].
  2. Create a work order with two lines: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in New Work Order pick Customer [Cust-1] and its Asset > Save. The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form open: in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line, turn Line Approved on (this makes the work order Approved) > Save & Add Line for the next line or Save & Close. Record the number shown as [WO-1]. Line names in this case (such as "Line 1") are only labels for you: the New Line form's "What Are You Doing?" box only offers ready-made lines (typed text finds no results), so pick any ready-made line for each one (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot") and write down which is which.
  3. Enter a tech story on Line 1 (any text) and save. Leave Line 2 without a story.
  4. Confirm [User-B]'s role: Settings > Roles & Permissions > the role > Work orders > View mode = Tech view. Sign [User-B] in in the second browser at the same location.
  5. Check the setup worked: on [WO-1]'s Lines tab, Line 1 shows its story and Line 2 has none; [User-B] can open [WO-1] in the second browser. If not, fix it before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open the work order [WO-1] and click the Lines tab.
  2. Look at both lines for any marker about the tech story (an icon, badge or colour).
  3. Repeat in the second browser (Tech View work order mode, as [User-B]).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Neither line shows any new marker in place of the removed check mark. Any required-story marker would need its own specification, so none ships with this change.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10051 (Story 8, Remove the tech story check-mark indicator); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S8-E1, read 8 Oct 2026. Source-verified 8 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)
